crowd.title: Agent ID Crowd
crowd.intro: The Agent ID Crowd combines every revealed forecast into one probability per question. Each Agent ID belongs to one verified person and cannot be transferred, so the crowd resists fake accounts.
crowd.methodTitle: Method v1 (to be pre registered before use)
method: Weights: max(0, prior shrunk skill) plus a small floor, using only rounds resolved before this round's commit deadline, so nothing leaks from the future.
Combination: a weighted mean in log odds space, optionally extremized with a factor chosen only on past rounds.
It is compared with the simple mean and the market. Whichever scores better on held out past rounds is kept, and that choice is pre registered.
Anyone can recompute every aggregate from chain data and the published snapshots.
crowd.honesty: The site always shows whether the crowd beats the market, even when it does not.

docs.title: Docs
docs.intro: How Forewit works, how it scores, and what its owner can and cannot do.

how.title: How it works
blocks: Forewit publishes one round of real questions each day. The questions come from Predict.fun prediction markets, the markets inside Binance Wallet.

list: Before the commit deadline, your agent sends a hidden hash of your probabilities. Nobody, including us, can read them.

In the last 15 minutes before the deadline (normally at 5 minutes), the order book mid price of each question is posted onchain in clear, once, as the baseline. The contract refuses it at any other time.
After the deadline, you reveal. The contract checks that the reveal matches your commit.
When the markets resolve onchain (Gnosis Conditional Tokens on BSC), the contract scores every forecast with the Brier rule and compares it with the baseline.

blocks: Your scores form a public track record tied to your Agent ID. An Agent ID is non transferable and limited to one per Binance user, so a track record cannot be bought, sold or faked with many wallets.
The Agent ID Crowd combines all revealed forecasts into one forecast per question. The site always shows whether it beats the market.

list: Probabilities are stored in basis points, from 0 to 10000. A Yes outcome is 10000 and a No outcome is 0.
Brier = (p minus outcome) squared. This site divides it by 100,000,000, so 0 is perfect and 1 is the worst possible. Lower is better.

Baseline Brier is the same formula applied to the market price: the order book mid price posted onchain in the last 15 minutes before the commit deadline. A round without a baseline is still scored, with skill 0.
Skill = baseline Brier minus your Brier. Positive skill means you beat the market price on that question.
Void questions (a split payout, a resolution seen before the round was sealed, or a question still unresolved after the reveal deadline plus the round's resolution wait) are skipped for everyone.
A commit that is never revealed is a forfeit: every non void question counts as the worst possible Brier. Revealing is never worse than forfeiting.
Score = sum of skill / (questions with a baseline + 20). The 20 pulls small samples toward zero skill.
To be ranked you need at least 5 scored rounds and 20 questions with a baseline. Sample size and participation rate are shown next to every score.
Rank uses skill against the market, never raw Brier. Raw Brier mostly measures how easy the questions were; skill rewards only information beyond the market price.
Raw Brier and calibration are shown as diagnostics and never used for rank.

selection.title: Question selection
blocks: Rule v3.1, pre registered on 23 Nov 2026. No sports and no politics questions. The keeper applies it mechanically and archives the raw market data and its output, so anyone can rerun it. A round never changes rules after it opens.

list: Binary and unresolved on one of the allowlisted Conditional Tokens contracts, with Yes as the first outcome.
No sports or esports markets.
Every non crypto question needs a two sided order book, a spread of at most 10 points and at least 100 USD of 24 hour volume.
At most one market per event.
Daily rounds: the daily crypto Up or Down markets plus liquid event markets, ending 6 to 72 hours after the commit deadline, 3 to 8 questions, resolution wait 7 days.
Long horizon rounds: liquid event markets ending more than 72 hours and at most 100 days after the deadline, resolution wait 120 days.

blocks: Every question is shown with its parent event question and its option, for example the event "Highest temperature in Shenzhen on November 24?" with the option "24°C". A question without an event question is never shown.

owner.title: Owner permissions
blocks: ForecastLedger is non upgradeable: no proxy, no selfdestruct, no delegatecall, no payable function. It holds no funds and no tokens and asks for no approvals.

list: ROUND_MANAGER can create rounds, choosing questions by the published selection rule (docs/QUESTION_SELECTION.md) and each round's resolution wait (1 to 120 days, fixed at creation and published before any commit), and can post the baseline once per round, only in the last 15 minutes before the commit deadline.
PAUSER can pause new commits and new rounds. Pause never blocks reveal, revealFor, seal, finalize, voidStale, score or forfeit.
DEFAULT_ADMIN can grant and revoke roles. Moving the admin seat itself takes two steps with a 1 day delay, and the pauser role moves with it.
edit or delete commits, reveals, outcomes or scores;
set a market outcome (outcomes come only from the Conditional Tokens payouts onchain, or Void);
move any asset, because the contract holds none.

blocks.h: Fixed forever at deploy (immutable, no setter exists)

list: AGENT_ID: the Agent ID contract used for the commit gate.
The allowlist of up to 4 Conditional Tokens contracts.

MIN_COMMIT_WINDOW and MIN_REVEAL_WINDOW: the shortest commit and reveal windows a round may have. On BSC mainnet (chain 56) the constructor refuses anything below 2 hours and 12 hours, and the mainnet deploy script fails before broadcasting if the configured windows are lower. Short windows exist only on test networks for fast end to end tests.
Maximum windows (7 days each), the resolution wait bounds (1 to 120 days), MAX_QUESTIONS (16), MAX_BATCH (100) and the commit hash scheme are compile time constants.

blocks: Move DEFAULT_ADMIN to a multisig, or renounce roles that are not essential. This will be announced before it happens.

security.title: Security and threat model
blocks: The full threat model names a defence and a test for every item. The main ones:

list: Copying others: commits are hashes over a 32 byte random salt, so nobody can read a forecast before the deadline.
Copying the market: skill is measured against the market price, so copying it scores about zero skill.
Selective reveal: an unrevealed commit is a forfeit with the worst possible Brier.
Cherry picking rounds: ranking needs 5 rounds and 20 questions, and shows participation.
Many identities: commit requires an Agent ID, one per Binance user. Residual risk: a person with two Binance accounts.
Early resolution: a question resolved before the round is sealed is Void for everyone.

Baseline manipulation: the baseline is posted in clear, once, only in the last 15 minutes before the deadline, the raw order books are archived, and the same baseline applies to everyone. Commits made after it was posted are recorded and can be flagged on the leaderboard.
Admin abuse: no upgrade path, and pause never blocks reveal or scoring.
Prompt injection: market titles and all API text are treated as untrusted data and shown as plain text.
This site: static files, read only, no wallet connection, no secrets, pinned dependencies and a strict Content Security Policy.

Leaked team key: the admin revokes the leaked keeper role instantly on both contracts and replaces the key; a leak can never edit a commit, reveal, outcome or score. Every key, who holds it and the response plan are in the docs under Keys, secrets and incidents.
Found a security problem? Report it privately through GitHub security advisories on the forewit repository, not in a public issue.

blocks: Status: independent reviews of the mainnet build and of ForewitScores (with its delta review) found no open High or Medium issue; the accepted residual risks are listed in the threat model. Both contracts are live on BSC mainnet and verified on BscScan and Sourcify.

One time setup, about two minutes. You need Node.js 22 or newer (nodejs.org). Your agent then reads rounds and prepares your forecast; your wallet still asks you to approve every send.

blocks.h: Local server: prepares transactions, never signs

list: Runs on your computer over stdio: npx forewit mcp
Tools: prepare_commit, prepare_reveal, prepare_profile, my_receipts.

prepare_commit makes a random salt, saves the reveal receipt in the .forewit folder of your home directory with owner only access, and returns the commit hash, the calldata and the exact baw contract call preview command. The salt is not returned to the agent.
prepare_reveal works only after the commit deadline, when the salt has to go onchain anyway.
my_receipts lists your receipts without salts. It returns salts only when you ask for a private backup, and only after the commit deadline.
It never signs, never sends and never runs the Binance Agentic Wallet. You preview and approve every transaction in your own wallet. Its only network access is the pinned public RPC.

prior.title: Prior art
blocks: Foresight Arena (arXiv 2605.00420, April 2026) is an onchain benchmark for AI forecasting agents. It runs commit reveal on Polygon over Polymarket questions, scores with Brier and the Murphy decomposition, and uses ERC8004 reputation. Our mechanism is close to theirs, and we say so openly.

The difference is identity. ERC8004 identities can be transferred and anyone can mint them, so a track record built on them can be bought, or faked with many identities. Agent ID is non transferable and limited to one per Binance user, which makes both the track record and the crowd forecast resistant to fake accounts.

BitPredict keeps a centralized, timestamped reputation for crypto predictions. Our difference: the record lives onchain, so nobody can fake or transfer it, and it is tied to a non transferable Agent ID.
Forewit is also built for people as well as agents, and uses the prediction markets already inside Binance Wallet.

list: ForecastBench: most forecasters scored worse than the market price they were given, so all skill is measured against the market.
Good Judgment Open: an improper scoring rule can be gamed, so we use only strictly proper rules.
Allora: weight the crowd by past skill.
Always show sample size, and compare forecasters with the crowd as well as the market.

blocks.strong: Forecasting scores only. Not financial advice. Forewit does not take bets, hold funds or pay returns. Prediction markets and crypto are risky and may be restricted in your region.

list: Forewit records forecasts and scores. It is not a betting product and pays nothing out.
Each commit and reveal costs network gas, paid by you.
Market prices shown here are information, not a recommendation to trade.
Check the rules where you live before using prediction markets.

faq.title: FAQ

blocks.h: Do I need an Agent ID?

blocks: Yes. On mainnet the contract accepts a commit only from a wallet that holds an Agent ID.
Only network gas. Every transaction has value 0. There are no deposits, entry fees or payouts.

blocks.h: What if I forget to reveal?

blocks: The round counts as a forfeit: every non void question gets the worst possible Brier. Keep your reveal receipt safe.
Nobody before the commit deadline. Revealed forecasts are public onchain. Your name appears on the leaderboard only if you opt in.

blocks.h: Can I look up someone else?

blocks: No. Only people who opted in are listed by name, and there is no search by name for anyone else.
Because the market price is hard to beat. Skill shows whether a forecast added information beyond it.

help.glossaryIntro: Every term and number this site uses, in plain words.

intro.home: How it works: each day Forewit opens a round of real questions from Predict.fun prediction markets. You, or your AI agent, commit a probability for each one, hidden until the deadline, and reveal it afterwards. When the markets settle, the contract scores your forecast against the market price, and every score adds to a public track record tied to your Agent ID.
intro.rounds: Each round is a small set of questions with a commit deadline and a reveal deadline. Open a round to see its questions and market prices, and after the commit deadline the revealed forecasts.
intro.round: Give a probability for each question below before the commit deadline, then reveal it before the reveal deadline. The square shows the market price, the diamond the crowd. Your score compares your forecast with the market price at the deadline.
intro.roundHidden: Forecasts stay hidden until the commit deadline. The revealed forecasts chart and the crowd forecast appear here as people reveal.
intro.play: What you need, and what happens in one round. For the exact commands, follow the Start page step by step.
intro.profile: To appear by name, opt in with the forewit profile command of the CLI; you confirm it in your wallet like any other transaction, and the off option removes your name again.
intro.docsOrder: New here? Read in this order: How to play, then How it works and Scoring. The rest go deeper, and every page links to the next one at the bottom.

help.scoresWhen: Round {n} is scored after its reveal deadline ({t}), once its markets settle onchain. Scores appear here then.

agentId.d: A non transferable identity, one per Binance user, claimed in the Binance App. The ledger accepts a commit only from a wallet that holds one, so one person builds one track record.

forecast.d: Your probability that a question resolves Yes, given as a percentage. The CLI takes whole numbers from 1 to 99, one per question.

commit.d: A hidden hash of your probabilities and a random secret (the salt), sent onchain before the commit deadline. Nobody, including Forewit, can read it until you reveal.

salt.d: The random secret inside your commit, saved in your reveal receipt on your computer. Keep it private until the commit deadline. Without it you cannot reveal.

reveal.d: After the commit deadline and before the reveal deadline you publish your probabilities and salt. The contract checks that they match your commit.

forfeit.d: A commit that was never revealed. Every non void question in that round counts as the worst possible Brier (1), so revealing is never worse than forfeiting.

market.d: The price of Yes on the Predict.fun market, read as a probability: 62% means the market gives Yes a 62% chance. Before the deadline the site shows the latest published price.

baseline.d: The order book mid price of each question, posted onchain once in the last 15 minutes before the commit deadline. Every forecaster in the round is compared with this same price.

crowd.d: All revealed forecasts on a question combined into one probability. It appears once forecasts are revealed, and the site shows whether it beats the market.

brier.d: How far a forecast was from what happened: (probability minus outcome) squared, with Yes as 1 and No as 0. 0 is perfect, always saying 50% gives 0.25, and 1 is the worst. Lower is better.

skill.d: Market Brier minus your Brier on the same question. Positive means you were closer to the outcome than the market price. The leaderboard adds it up and divides by (questions with a baseline + 20), so a handful of questions counts for little.

calibration.d: How far your probabilities are from how often things happened, over 10 ranges: of your 70% forecasts, did about 70% resolve Yes? Lower is better. Shown for information only, never used for rank.

participation.d: Rounds revealed divided by rounds committed, counting only rounds whose reveal window has closed.

ranked.d: A public forecaster is ranked after at least 5 scored rounds and 20 questions with a baseline. Before that they are listed under Not yet ranked.

questionsCol.d: Questions with a market baseline that were scored for this forecaster, and the number of rounds scored or forfeited.

dagger.d: Part of this skill came from commits made after the baseline was posted.

commitsOpen.d: The round takes commits until its commit deadline. All forecasts stay hidden.

revealWindow.d: The commit deadline has passed. Everyone who committed reveals before the reveal deadline.

resolving.d: Reveals are closed. The round waits for its markets to settle onchain and for every commit to be scored.

scored.d: Every question has an outcome and every commit is scored or forfeited.

commits.d: How many forecasts were committed in this round. Each comes from a wallet that holds an Agent ID.

revealProgress.d: How many of the commits have been revealed so far.

void.d: Unresolved: the market has not settled yet. Void: the question is skipped for everyone, after a split payout, a resolution seen before the round was sealed, or no result after the reveal deadline plus the resolution wait.

resolutionWait.d: How long after the reveal deadline the round waits for its markets to settle. A question still unsettled after that becomes Void. Fixed when the round is created.

selectionRule.d: The published rule the keeper used to pick this round’s questions from Predict.fun markets: no sports, no politics, liquid markets only.

histogram.d: How many revealed forecasts fell in each 10 point range, with the market at deadline and the crowd marked. n is the number of revealed forecasts.

distinct.d: Different wallets that have committed at least once, across all rounds.

ledger.d: The Forewit contract on BSC that records commits, reveals, baselines, outcomes and scores. It holds no funds and cannot be upgraded.

ctf.d: The onchain contract where Predict.fun markets settle. Outcomes come only from its payouts, so nobody, including Forewit, can set a result.

resolvedCount.d: Questions whose outcome has been read from the Conditional Tokens payouts, out of all questions so far.

holders.d: Distinct wallets that sent at least one commit. Only Agent ID holders can commit, so each one is a holder.
